summary: Iteration 22 — Verified BOTH fixes for the 'PDF documents are not the same ones loaded' regression. BACKEND (pytest 4/4 in /app/backend/tests/test_iteration22_pdf_unicode_and_auth.py): (1) GET /api/documents/10cac2c3-2c17-4e7e-ab35-146d4c60e190/stamped (em-dash titled 'Policy & Procedure Handbook — Sister to Sister, PHCP', U+2014 in title) returns 200 application/pdf with a real %PDF body (~21 MB). (2) Content-Disposition header is RFC-5987 compliant: contains BOTH a classic ASCII-only filename="..." form AND a filename*=UTF-8''<percent-encoded> form. (3) Sanity over a mix of non-ASCII and ASCII titled docs returns 200 PDFs for every probed id. (4) 5 different doc ids → 5 distinct SHA-256 hashes (no cached blob, backend serves correct file per id). FRONTEND (Playwright, mobile 390x844, preview URL, fresh localStorage/sessionStorage clear between auth modes): Supabase mode login (admin@healthguard.com / AdminPassword123!) lands on dashboard (stat-documents=50). Documents tab renders 27 view-doc-* buttons in the initial FlatList window. Opened 3 different docs via view-doc-<id> taps; PdfViewerModal rendered each with a UNIQUE title and a UNIQUE iframe blob: URL (3/3 unique titles, 3/3 unique blob srcs) — proves the modal no longer re-uses a stale blob between opens. Network capture (page.on('request')) on every /api/documents/{id}/stamped initiated by the modal showed Authorization: Bearer <870-char token> (a Supabase ES256 JWT, fetched via getAuthToken()) on ALL 3 calls; all 3 returned HTTP 200 with content-type application/pdf — proves api/client.ts.getAuthToken() picks up the Supabase access token (the original root cause was the 6 callsites reading legacy AsyncStorage 'userToken' which is empty in Supabase mode, sending 401s, and the modal then rendering the previous blob). Assistant tab: sending 'hello' returned a 191-char non-error response ('Hello! I'm HealthGuard, your compliance assistant…') — proves the assistant.tsx auth helper fix. Legacy mode (toggle pill → 'Auth: Legacy (MongoDB)', Admin@123) login succeeded and the dashboard rendered. PARTIAL GAP: the em-dash card and 3 other targeted ids did not get opened via the UI because they were beyond the FlatList's virtualized window (27 view-doc buttons present in DOM, ~38 with storage_path total) and the Playwright mouse.wheel scroll on the web-rendered FlatList did not materialize them. Those 3 targets and the legacy-mode UI tap on the em-dash card are NOT regressions of the fix — they are a harness limitation. The em-dash + 5-id uniqueness assertions are independently proven at the HTTP layer in pytest, and the Authorization-header assertion is proven on 3 doc opens in the Supabase UI run.

rca_of_issue: USER SYMPTOM: 'PDF documents are not the same ones loaded'. TWO simultaneous root causes (both addressed in this iteration). RC#1 BACKEND: server.py routes for /api/documents/{id}/stamped and the packet stamped endpoint built `Content-Disposition: inline; filename="{title}.pdf"` with the raw title. Starlette serialises response headers as Latin-1; any non-ASCII glyph (em-dash, smart quotes, accents — common in seed data like 'Policy & Procedure Handbook —') raised UnicodeEncodeError mid-response → the server returned 500 with no body. RC#2 FRONTEND: PdfViewerModal and 5 other callsites called AsyncStorage.getItem('userToken') directly. In Supabase mode (the default after Phase 6 cutover) that key is empty, so requests went out without Authorization → backend 401 (HTML/JSON). The modal's old error path swallowed the failure and the iframe kept showing the previously-loaded blob — literally a different document than the one the user tapped. The 401 also masked the backend 500 above, so users couldn't tell which doc actually failed. FIX (both shipped together): (a) server.py:33-46 added _safe_disposition() emitting RFC 5987 Content-Disposition with both ASCII-only filename= (non-ASCII → '_') AND filename*=UTF-8'' percent-encoded; used on both stamped routes (lines 774, 1430). (b) api/client.ts exports getAuthToken() (Supabase access token first, legacy userToken second, null third) and getAuthHeaders(); migrated all 6 callsites + a content-type guard in PdfViewerModal so error bodies can no longer be rendered as PDFs. VERIFICATION: backend pytest 4/4 PASS (em-dash 200, header has both filename forms, 5-id SHA-256 all distinct, mixed ASCII/non-ASCII all 200). Frontend Playwright Supabase mode: 3 different doc opens → 3 unique titles + 3 unique blob URLs, all 3 stamped calls carried Bearer token (~870 chars, Supabase JWT) and returned 200 application/pdf. Assistant tab also returned a non-error response in Supabase mode (proves the same getAuthToken fix on assistant.tsx). MITIGATION FOR REGRESSION: keep _safe_disposition as the only path that writes a Content-Disposition with arbitrary user-supplied text; ban direct AsyncStorage.getItem('userToken') reads outside AuthContext.tsx bootstrap.
